title: Gabber's degree-zero criterion for etale sheaves of sets
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose that for every sheaf of sets $G$ on the underlying Zariski space of $X$, the canonical restriction $\Gamma(X,G)\to\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}_{\mathrm{Zar}}G)$ is bijective, with topological inverse image as in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. Suppose also that for every finite morphism $h:X'\to X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], the same assertion holds for the base-changed closed immersion $i':Z'=Z\times_XX'\to X'$ and every Zariski sheaf of sets on $X'$. Then for every sheaf of sets $F$ on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $X$, the canonical restriction $\Gamma(X,F)\to\Gamma(Z,i^{-1}_{\mathrm{et}}F)$ is bijective, where $i^{-1}_{\mathrm{et}}$ is etale inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

proof.text: Use the Zariski-injectivity consequence for i with hZar to obtain injectivity of the étale unit at the identity object.

For an arbitrary section t of the inverse image, choose a finite surjective h and s\prime from the finite-lift theorem. Its first equality is exactly the descent equalizer condition; finite surjective descent gives s on X with h^*s=s\prime.

The unit at any terminal étale object is injective for a finite surjection: transport its sections to the identity object using the unique terminal isomorphism and use naturality and finite descent injectivity. Base change preserves terminal objects, so this applies to the pullback of the identity along i. Composing the unit with the composition comparison and fibre-product pasting isomorphism preserves injectivity.

The composition-unit equation, followed by the inverse fibre-product pasting map, identifies the comparison of a pulled-back section with the unit of the composite morphism. On the closed base change, its finite surjective projection has injective comparison. Apply that injectivity to i^*s and t. The second equality of the finite lift, h^*s=s\prime, and the two composition-unit identities make their comparisons equal. Transport along the pullback square equation is checked by equality induction. Hence i^*s=t and restriction is surjective.
